neet_phy_u19_t03_1.working: An LED emits light when electrons and holes recombine at the junction. This needs carrier injection, which happens only under forward bias.

neet_phy_u19_t03_3.working: Si has Eg ≈ 1.1 eV, which corresponds to infrared, not visible light. It is also an indirect band gap material, so radiative recombination is inefficient.

neet_phy_u19_t03_4.working: A: photon energy ≈ Eg (IV). B: typical LED reverse breakdown is about 5 V (III). C: red LED threshold is about 1.8 V (I). D: blue LED threshold is about 3 V (II).

neet_phy_u19_t03_5.working: A is true (radiative recombination of injected carriers). B is false: 620 nm photons have lower energy, so they need a lower threshold voltage than 450 nm. C is true (intensity rises with current, then saturates). D is true (NCERT describes LEDs as heavily doped p-n junctions). E is false (breakdown is only about 5 V). Correct set: A, C, D.
